utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. It seems the weather defeated us this morning. Could I mention before I turn to Mr. Whiting that I was too hasty yesterday as we adjourned in indicating that we could not sit on Friday week because of a plenary sitting. It now appears that plenary will not commence until the middle of the day so that we will be able to sit until about noon on Friday the 11th. So that we will get some useful sitting out of the day. I see the Defence bench is up to near strength.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May I just say I'm really grateful to Your Honours and also, may I say, to Mr. Whiting for accommodating the difficulties that I had and it's been a very important time. So thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Whiting, you were wanting to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There was a matter that arose yesterday that I -- and I've had discussions with Defence counsel about this matter that I think requires some clarification. At the beginning of the session with respect to the application that Mr. Topolski made, I represented that the OTP had not told this witness, Mr. Qeriqi, anything about a change in status, that he had not been told that he was no longer a suspect. That was true when I said it yesterday and from our point of view it is true today. I double-checked it just to be absolutely sure and just from our point of view no such representation has been made to this witness. He has not been told that he is not a suspect. Now, to make the record complete and clear, I should say that the investigator who was mentioned by the witness, Mr. Lehtinen, Ole Lehtinen, has had significant discussions with this witness about coming here to testify in this trial as a witness. Once the trial started he did have contact with him about coming here, about him requiring a subpoena before he would come here to testify. Mr. Lehtinen was there when he was served with the subpoena to come testify as a witness, and he has been involved in his arrangements to come here to testify as a witness. So that is true. However he has not been told by Mr. Lehtinen or as far as I know, and I've checked very carefully, by anyone in the OTP that he is not a suspect and I thought it was important to make that clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Only -- yes, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm sorry I interrupted Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was about to say something but wisdom would get me to hold my tongue until I've heard you. Wisdom is a rare quality with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, of course the bar accepts what Mr. Whiting says, no doubt faithfully reporting that was what he was told; however, this is a matter of potentially some significance. And I simply say this: that we would expect and we would hope that the at the appropriate time Mr. Lehtinen is made available again for further cross-examination upon this and indeed upon other matters that have arisen and I have no doubt will arise regarding the conduct of the investigation. And I shall say no more than that on that subject. May I also while I'm on my feet beg your forgiveness and leave. There was a matter that I should have put to Mr. Qeriqi yesterday by way of detail in relation to something I've always had instructions about. I omitted to do so. Before Mr. Mansfield starts his cross-examination, may I be permitted to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. What I had been about to say was that that issue does not affect the decision we reached on your motion yesterday, Mr. Topolski. The only evidence we presently have on the issue is that of the witness who has said he was told that he was no longer a suspect. So if the Prosecution wants to advance the factual material in any way, it will need to give consideration to further evidence. And yes, you may have leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh, I was hoping we would get a witness in before we finish today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The door is half open, only half. It relates to this very same issue because I was hoping to ask this witness a little bit more about what he's already said in relation to not being told that he was, or being told that he wasn't -- put it that way round -- being told that he wasn't a suspect. Now, if it's going to be suggested that in fact that's wrong, he's never been told, then before -- it would be useful certainly and desirable before I ask further questions, if there's any documentation about the meetings that have just been described with Mr. Lehtinen about coming here to testify, subpoenaed and so forth, then it would be of use to us to know what in fact he is going to be -- if Mr. Lehtinen is going to return to the Tribunal to deal with these matters, what he's likely to be saying while the witness is still here. So I merely indicate that, and I give notice I'm going to ask a number of questions about this because it will bear upon your ability in the end and your function of assessing the truth of this witness. So I merely ask, if there's any material may we have it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, are you in a position to assist in that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Not on the -- not at the moment, that is I can't -- I cannot answer if there are -- the question if there are notes about these meetings or reports or anything. It wouldn't take me long to determine that. I'll just need to ask the investigator, but it would take me, say, ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would suggest that you get those inquiries underway and arrange to communicate them to Mr. Mansfield as soon as you -- the result as soon as you can. And in the meantime, we will move on. It seems to me that the question whether or not you propose to recall Mr. Lehtinen is one which you would normally evaluate at the end of the cross-examination of this witness rather than on your feet now. And if you haven't a clear view about that at the moment, we would not press you further.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I do not have a clear view about that. Your Honour is correct it's something that I have to evaluate later. And I can with modern technology I think from my seat here make this inquiry to Mr. Lehtinen, assuming he's at his desk, and hopefully get the answer relatively quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, with or without technology if you could help Mr. Mansfield as soon as possible and before he commits himself down a course he may not want to commit himself to, it would be useful for everybody. The witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Qeriqi. If I could remind you of the affirmation which you took at the beginning of your evidence; that still applies. I'm sorry you've had to wait longer, but apparently the weather conditioned delayed the arrival of the accused this morning. Now, Mr. Topolski has one matter that he wants to raise with you and then Mr. Mansfield will have some questions. Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm very grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, you want to say something.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have a request. Yesterday there were cases when we went on a closed session. I request that this Trial Chamber when Defence counsel are cross-examinating [as interpreted] not to go on a closed session. I want people, my people back home, to be informed correctly about everything. So my question is not to go on closed session. I want everything to be open and public. I want everyone to know what the lawyer is asking because I am going back to Kosova. I really hope that my request will be taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for the indication of your willingness to speak openly and for others to hear everything that you say and the questions you're asked. That certainly is relevant and is taken into account. The Chamber, though, has to consider the possibility that others may be affected by what you say, particularly when you name other people. And in some cases, that will require or may require that small aspects of your evidence be in closed session. As you will appreciate, almost all of your evidence to date has been in open session. If the occasion arises, we will consider and take into account the view and wish that you have expressed. Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, you'll remember yesterday we were talking about the formation of battalions and brigades. I wonder if you can help me with a meeting that I suggest you attended. First of all, when it was. The best I can do is to suggest to you that it must have been in the first ten days or so of August of 1998. Secondly, I suggest - and I'm going to break it up and invite you to deal with each part of this - secondly I suggest that Isak Musliu, Qerqizi, came to Kroimire to tell you of an important meeting that was going to take place that evening, and the meeting was to take place in Klecka at a house where Fatmir Limaj was based. Now, do you recollect any of this?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned it earlier that up to the offensive, up to the end of May, number one was Shukri Buja and I was his deputy, number two. After the offensive, the battalion and the brigade was formed and the decision was taken, the decision that I brought here, according to which I was appointed a battalion commander. For the period prior to this, I said that I rarely went to Klecka and I'm not able to know whether there was a brigade or not. Maybe Shukri might know this. It is true that -- and the reason why I brought that document is that I became a commander, battalion commander, after the offensive. And from that time, from my appointment, I became an official leader of the staff in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: The offensive you're referring to is the offensive in late July by the Serbs, isn't it? Let's get that clear first of all.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The offensive occurred on the 25th and 26th of July, and I mean this offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Right. Yes. Now, I'm being very specific, Mr. Qeriqi, or trying to be and I'd like, sir, if you could to see if you can help me. I'm suggesting that you attended a meeting in Klecka in a house where Fatmir Limaj was based in the first few days of August. This was a house located about halfway up a hill in Klecka. Did you attend a meeting in Klecka in early August 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly whether it was beginning or the end of August, but I was there. It is true that I attended that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Right. I'm going to give you a list of people who were also there. Isak Musliu was there. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you give me the list with all the persons because I might not remember that meeting, so it's easier for me to have all the persons that attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Right. Very well. It's not many. Isak Musliu, Fatmir Limaj, you, Skender Hoti, Muse Jashari, Ismet Jashari, and possibly one or two others who I'm afraid I cannot identify.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, yes. It is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: This meeting began by discussing the situation with regard to civilians and then moved quickly on to discuss the new brigade structure, and the meeting lasted about one and a half to two hours. Do you recollect?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember how long it lasted, but as a meeting I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: And there is one particularly and extraordinary incident that occurred at the end of it that I suggest may bring it back to your mind, Mr. Qeriqi, and it was this: Just as the meeting was breaking up and people were leaving, three artillery rounds were fired by the Serbs into the garden of the house. Now do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but it could be that this happened during the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: And it was from that meeting that it was decided, amongst other things, that Fatmir Limaj should become the commander of 121st Brigade and as you have indicated in due course you were to become appointed as commander of a battalion within that brigade. So that was the meeting where these matters were resolved, I suggest. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that the issue who will become commander was discussed during this meeting, but at that time I did -- I was appointed commander of the battalion. I did take the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to Your Honours for permitting me to put that, and I apologise for not putting it last night.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Qeriqi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Topolski. Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I have an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The answer to the question is there are no substantive reports of the meetings. There is a record -- these were just courtesy meetings to arrange travel and coming -- being a witness. There are -- there is a record of when the meetings occurred, but the there is no substance to record. So there's no report about the meeting, just a record of when the meetings occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, good morning. I'm sorry about --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry about the delay. I represent Fatmir Limaj, who sits behind here, who you know or you knew him as Celiku. I want to ask --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: -- you some questions that relate to what -- the matter that Mr. Whiting has just raised. This relates to something you said yesterday, and may I just indicate what you said yesterday concerning whether you had been told you were a suspect or not. That's the topic. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that when I was summoned to be questioned I was allegedly a suspect and allegedly had knowledge about things that happened. After the questioning and after I told what I knew -- as for other matters they surely realised that I was not familiar with and most probably that suspect quality was removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What you said yesterday was this: That you had not been told that in writing, but a person called Ole you tend to forget his name - and I am going to quote exactly what you said - "When we met with him, he told me that after the investigation they conducted they found out that I was not a suspect, and this was in the end before I came here." Now, do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say this and you know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Just one second. Just listen to the questions, it may be a bit quicker. I want to ask some more questions about this. First of all, I know it's difficult because of the lapse of time. Your interview, when it was indicated that you were a suspect, was in April 2003.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on 23rd of April, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How long after that was it that you had the meeting with the investigator called Ole? Can you tell -- can you give us some idea?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take notes and I haven't written the date down, but it was most probably two or three other times that I met with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where did you meet?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pristina where their offices are, in their office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When you met him on these two or three occasions, was he on his own?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And anyone else?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And were you on your own?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, you didn't keep a note, but did the investigator so far as you could tell while you were in his presence, did he make any notes?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I apologise for asking you the detail, but it may be important. Do you happen to know -- remember whether the notes that he made were in a notebook, on loose sheets of paper, a file, or was he doing it on a laptop?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think it was on -- in a notebook. It could be possible that he made notes somewhere else, but I really didn't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Now, can you remember on which of the two or three occasions that he told you that you were no longer a suspect? Do you think it was the first or the second or the last meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the meeting before the last. I'm not quite sure, but I think it was the meeting before the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, at that meeting before the last one, was anything else discussed with you besides the fact that you were no longer a suspect?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't discussed, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Nothing else was discussed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked whether I would come to this trial and -- as a witness, and my reply was that I was ready to come and testify about myself and about my knowledge on the KLA war. And what I know is that it was a just war and it is a great satisfaction for me to come and testify about this war. In the end, this request was an obligatory one, but as I said from the very beginning I made it clear that I was ready to come here voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, either on that occasion, the meeting before the last one, or the last meeting were you ever told that the Prosecutor or the prosecuting authority did not regard you as someone telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Either at the meeting we've just talked about, the one before the last one, or on the last meeting you had with Ole Lehtinen, the investigator, did Ole ever suggest to you that you were not regarded as someone telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't say this to me. He didn't say that I was not regarded as someone telling the truth. On the contrary, he believed that I was telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you did come here very recently, did you have a meeting here in The Hague with any member of the prosecuting team before you actually began your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met with the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Is that the same investigator you have been referring to as Ole?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the one who is here, the one who questioned me on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I think you mean Mr. Whiting, who sits across this Tribunal floor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, did he say to you before you gave evidence, Look here, we don't think you're telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm sorry to have taken some time on this topic, but today the Tribunal has been informed that the investigator you call Ole is denying that he ever said these things to you. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him telling me that I was not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What is being denied further is that you were ever told that you were not a suspect; in other words, are you aware at the moment that the Prosecution are going to suggest you are a suspect? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I would object to that question. That's -- that is not quite right. The issue is not whether he is a suspect or not; the issue is what he has been told about his status. And I would ask that the question be put clearly to him if it's going to be put to him this way, that Mr. Lehtinen has said that he has not told him that he was -- that his status has changed and he has not told him anything about not being a suspect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I'll ask you the questions to -- in stages. The investigator you are naming as Ole is saying that he never told you that your status has changed and that you were no longer a suspect. That's what he is now saying. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he did not give it to me in writing, maybe it's a misunderstanding. Maybe he said, In the beginning you were a suspect because you know many things, and I always thought that like any other investigator he is looking for something more. He wants me to say something more and maybe that he thought that I was not telling him everything. But Ole said that, You were a suspect but now you are no longer a suspect. There is no suspicion. In the beginning we thought that you knew many other things that you were not going to tell us. So this was it. Nonetheless, I did say things that I knew and I did come here to defend my statements from earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And while you have been here in this Tribunal, have you told the truth?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to give you the opportunity of dealing with in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. general terms what the allegations were that made them think, that is the prosecuting authority, in the beginning that you were a suspect. Do you follow what I'm going to do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat it once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I want to give you the opportunity now of dealing with in open session the allegations that were being made against you during the interview where it was being said you were a suspect. Do you follow what I'm about to do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You follow. The allegations in general terms - and I will not mention any names so we can remain in open session - the allegations were that first of all you authorised abductions and kidnapping of Serbs and Serb collaborators. Did you do any such thing?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never did such a thing. These allegations were made on the basis that I allegedly took them and brought them somewhere else, but in fact this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And the allegation in relation to that was that you were present when people were abducted or kidnapped. Were you ever present, if such a thing happened?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never present. I was never present and I never even heard that people were kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you authorise any arrests, as opposed to kidnapping, any arrests of Serbs or Serb alleged collaborators for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In the area for which you were or had some responsibility in your municipality, as far as you were aware were is there any detention or prison facilities?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where? In which zone?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to be careful about the use of the word "zone." In the area where you were acting on behalf of the KLA between April and August, that time span and that area. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was not in a position to think about prisons. This is really a funny question for me because at that time we could hardly find bread for us to feed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about a particular person who has made allegations to this Tribunal about you, and I am respecting your desire for open session; however, as His Honour has already pointed out to you, it isn't always possible to do everything in open session when identification of other people is at risk. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This worries me a lot, simply because of the fact that I live there, for some people that you asked me questions about, I do see and meet their families and I don't have any problems with them and simply they will not be put in any risk. And to put it shortly, lies should be made clear and -- I want the people there to know everything because otherwise how can the truth come out? But I know it is up for the Trial Chamber to decide on these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just indicate what I would like to do, and I appreciate what the witness says. I'm only going to take one example, but it's an example you may yourself recall. It occurred on Day 24. I'm not going to name who it was, but he -- this person gave evidence which implicated this witness. It's not been put to him and I would like it put to him so this witness can deal with it to the witness that also affects the person I represent. And what I would seek to do is to put the passages from the transcript where this witness is mentioned, but it was all in closed session when it was done originally. And plainly I don't want to transgress that original position. It's not for a desire that the truth should not come out in the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we must start in closed session, Mr. Mansfield. If we judge that that can be relaxed, we will intervene and change it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm much obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you very much for going into open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, if I may, I want to summarise in open session without naming anyone what the allegation was so you can say it in open session. The allegation is that you had ordered an individual to be brought to you in order to hand over weapons and that when the individual arrived in your presence a sack was put over his head and he was kidnapped. Is there any truth in that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no truth in that. I recounted even earlier with respect to that person. I think the police, too, asked me twice about this case; the investigators did also. We engaged in the same questions and answered the same talk. And I am repeating, this is not true. The truth is they came there of their own free will. One left in the direction of Shale, the other went home. After the war that old man asked to meet me and I told him, you can meet me any time because I have told the truth and I will uphold that truth. No sack. Nothing like that happened. Since I didn't know them before, that was the first time I saw them that day, and how could I do that? As far as I know this witness has said, from what I heard, I went to ask for Luan because I didn't find him. He was in the front line and that he had found my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May I just pick up one point in that answer. Can you help us as to which police had asked you twice about this particular incident? Which police was it? Which police force was it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The international police force in Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And sorry to be particular, but can you help us as to when it was that you were asked twice about this. Is it in 1999? 2000? 2001?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the war. I don't know, it was 2000 -- once in 2000, once in 2001 I think. I'm not sure but I know that it was after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And were the police officers who actually asked you the same on those two occasions or different police officers?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Again, this is for the purpose of the record. Forgive me, it's more detail. Do you recollect whether the police officers on those two occasions made a record, either wrote it down, what you were saying, or typed it up or put it on a laptop or whatever?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they wrote it down and I signed it myself; it was on a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Is it too much to ask you if you happen to know their names? Do you know the names of either of these people who spoke to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I forgot their name because it didn't seem important to me to remember the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to pass to a different topic. I want to ask a little bit about Fatmir Limaj himself and your contact with him. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, firstly would it be right to say that -- and I'm going to be specific about the time so you don't have to, as it were, range over a number of months. I am dealing with the period between April and August of 1998, the spring to summer period. I'm just dealing with that period. Now, you've indicated that you saw Fatmir Limaj or Celiku from time to time, but this morning you've indicated that you didn't go to Klecka very much until after you were appointed on the 16th of August. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, as I already explained, we met in Likovc as far as I remember. And from there we came together down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I was very rarely before the offensive in Klecka, compared to the period when I became a commander because I was not the top man. I was second in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, during that period before you were appointed in August --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And could we just have on the ELMO, please, P155. I think it should be a piece of paper on which the word "decision" is written. No. Yes, it's another sheet. I think it may be the one -- can we have the sheet on the ELMO which has got the word "decision" -- no, that's it. This is the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'll come to August in a moment. You see this is -- you have already talked about this. This is dated the 16th of August, 1998, signed by Celiku. Would it be right to say that in the April-to-August period on the occasions when you did meet Celiku there was never any discussion between you about detention camps or prisons? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be right. We never talked about such things. I cannot even imagine such a topic of conversation; it never occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In that period would it also be right to say that Celiku in fact never gave you any orders, did he?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained here that after this decision I reported in writing. Every week we held a meeting. But before the offensive it was Shukri, the commander, and I had to report to him on the situation on the stage of the positions as we were building. And it was very rarely that I went to Klecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Is it also right to say that you were unaware of who had appointed Shukri Buja. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated yesterday it must have been the General Staff. He couldn't come there on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Did you know who was on the General Staff between April and August? Did you know at that time who was on it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't need to say anything. Jakup Krasniqi, the spokesperson, informed you of all these things. So it's none of my business and I don't have any reason to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. So does it also follow - and you gave evidence to this effect yesterday and also on an earlier day this week - that so far as Mr. Buja was concerned, Shukri Buja was concerned, you did not know whether or if he got orders from anyone else and if he did who he got them from.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You might ask him in person. How can I speak on his behalf? I think he can tell you better than me because I informed him -- I reported to him about the positions, about the soldiers. And probably he had to report this to someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I want to ask you now finally about another topic, and this is about the development of the KLA as an army, as an organisation. It's about its development. Do you follow? That's the topic. And I want to suggest to you that the KLA in 1998 went through three very different and distinct phases. Are you following what I'm putting to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The first phase which had existed before April 1998 was an underground army which might be termed a guerrilla force, which undertook specific targeted operations on behalf of the community. Now, in other words, a guerrilla force. Do you agree with that description?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 14th of June when we went on a frontal attack, it was no longer guerrilla warfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I'll come to -- please be patient, I'm doing it slowly in phases. Phase one, do you agree it could be aptly or appropriately described as a guerrilla force, which then developed into a volunteer army with many people volunteering and coming forward to form units and points in various areas of Kosovo? So it's a volunteer army in about June/July. That's phase number two; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm repeating it, that it was a voluntary army until 1999 and everybody joined it on a voluntary basis. Nobody was forced to join it; that is true. But on the 14th of June I said we came out openly as an army. It was a frontal war. I mentioned this on the first day. It was a joy for us to join the KLA, to become a soldier of it, no matter what kind of weapons we had, just because we wanted to drive away the Serbs. And we did fight against tanks, many of them. So you cannot describe it as a guerrilla war; it was a frontal warfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I accept that. And what began to happen in August with the decision of your appointment on the 16th of August was that the volunteer army in various areas of Kosovo had to be organised and formalised into something more resembling an army that might be recognised in the rest of Europe. Do you follow the point I'm making?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. There were many internationals at that time who came and conducted negotiations and things like that, but I was on a lower rank so I didn't take part in this negotiations and talks. So I cannot give you an answer to what you are trying to put to me regarding those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, I don't want to ask you about negotiations. Thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mansfield. It's probably a convenient time, Mr. Whiting, to have a break. So we will have the first morning break now and resume at 20 minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 11.22 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, you'll be grateful to know I just have a few follow-up questions. I want to ask you about your conversations with Mr. Lehtinen to see if I can possibly clear up that matter. You said this morning when you started being asked about this topic - and I refer to page 10 of the transcript - you said: "I think that when I was summoned to be questioned I was allegedly a suspect and allegedly had knowledge about things that happened. After the questioning, and after I told what I knew -- as for other matters they surely realised that I was not familiar with and most probably that suspect quality was removed." And then later on on page 14 after some more questioning about this topic you said that you thought perhaps there was a misunderstanding about your conversations with Mr. Lehtinen. So my question is: Is it possible that you after time passed and after you were not charged with any crime, is it possible that in fact there was a misunderstanding and you were not actually told that your status had changed by Mr. Lehtinen but that's what you believed. Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was distracted. I've got to confess to the precise tone of the question. A reliability authority suggests that it may have been leading, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I submit that it wasn't. I'm just asking if something -- if it was possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let me re-read it then. No, I will now that question, Mr. Guy-Smith. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you need me to repeat the question, Mr. Qeriqi?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was rather hard for me to understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. I will repeat it, but not the whole thing. You said this morning that -- when you were first asked about your conversations with Mr. Lehtinen you said that after the questioning and "after I told what I knew -- as for other matters they surely realised that I was not familiar with and most probably that suspect quality was removed." Then you said later that you thought perhaps there was a misunderstanding about your conversations with Mr. Lehtinen. So my question is: Is it possible that after time passed and you were not charged with any crime, is it possible that in fact there was a misunderstanding and you were not actually told that your status had changed by Mr. Lehtinen, but that is what you believed? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. When you first questioned me as a suspect, it was, I believe, your way of questioning me or anyone because if you hadn't mentioned the word "suspect" perhaps I wouldn't have responded at all. It was later that I realised, myself, that you no longer suspected of me, even though here in the first session I saw that you still came back to that point or that implication or that you asked again. And I consider it normal. This is what I thought, as you said, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you have said that -- you have said that if the word "suspect" had not been mentioned, perhaps you would not have responded at all. So that leads me to this question --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this for the first time here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, I just was repeating what you said. So this leads me to this question: Does the fact -- has the fact that you were initially questioned and you were told you were a suspect and in court here today you've said you believe you're no longer a suspect, has that changed in any way your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. Like, there is -- how can I change it? I have come here to stand by what I said earlier and to tell the truth regarding KLA, the work that was done then. I said even earlier that I'm very happy and proud to be able to say what I know and what we did in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now I want to follow-up on that answer that you just have given. Mr. Qeriqi, focusing just for a moment on the four months of April, May, June, and July of 1998, is it important to you that the history of the KLA during those four months in your area be accurately told? Is that something that's important to you or is that not important to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it is important to me, when many people laid down their lives. And for the sake of the blood they have shed, I have told the truth and I am telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And is it -- is the fact that it is important to you that the history of that time period be accurately told, is that fact one of the reasons that you were willing to testify here today and in previous days to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is why I'm here, and before coming here I talked at length with my comrades. Everyone asked me to tell the truth, both the families of the martyrs, the true fighters who today are in the streets without a job. And I've spoken here also on their behalf as well as on my own behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Qeriqi, have you accused anybody in the KLA of committing any crimes during the war?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not accused anyone, and I haven't seen anyone committing any crimes. To my recollection, I have not accused anyone; I've just told the truth about KLA, of what I have seen with my eyes and what I have seen it do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Qeriqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, you'll be pleased to know that that's the end of the questions for you. The Tribunal would thank you for your assistance in coming here and for the evidence that you have given. You may now return to your home and carry on with your normal affairs. So thank you very much. You're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it over? Can I say a word, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask this Trial Chamber, with due respect for it, to judge the truth and only the truth and not be a political trial. I thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We're ready for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Would you please make the affirmation, reading it aloud, that's on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you understand me clearly?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you state your name, please.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: My name is Shukri Buja. I am from Bujan village, Lipjan municipality. I was born on the 27th of August, 1966.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you some questions about your background, but first I want to ask you a few preliminary questions. Did you receive a subpoena from the Court to testify here today in this trial?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive a subpoena to report to this court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, did you testify in the trial of Slobodan Milosevic on the 5th and 6th of June, 2002?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you subpoenaed to testify in that trial?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. I came here as a Prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you testified in the trial of Slobodan Milosevic on the 5th and 6th of June, 2002, did you tell the truth during your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, I told the truth under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, Mr. Buja, was that testimony largely about events that occurred in Racak in January of 1999?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before -- before you gave that testimony, had you been interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor in August, September, and October of 2001 concerning those matters?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in that statement that you gave to the OTP, were you truthful?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I tried to recollect all those events and to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask the witness to stand closer to the mike, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think the usher is going to ask you, sir -- try to bring you a little closer to the microphone and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you could try to speak a little bit louder, it will be easier for us to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Finally, sir, after you testified in the Milosevic case, were you summonsed to an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 28th of April, 2003?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you tell the truth in that interview?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I need to give -- to make an explanation regarding this interview, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you could first just answer the question and then provide your explanation. Did you -- did you tell the truth in that interview of April 2003, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I cannot say yes or no because I never saw the interview later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm not asking if you saw the interview later. What I'm asking is: When you went to the interview, did you try to tell the truth in response to the questions that were put to you? Were you trying to be truthful or were you untruthful?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: At that time I couldn't recollect the events accurately and thought that the same procedure would be followed as the investigator told me when I testified for the Milosevic case, when I met the investigator after the invitation I received in April of 2003 they told me that the same procedure would be followed. That's why in that statement I wasn't very focused, thinking that the same procedure would be followed and I would have occasion to review my statement and reformulate and correct mistakes if there were so that when I came before this Tribunal I could be truthful and speak truthfully under the oath. That's why I cannot speak about that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I appreciate that explanation, Mr. Buja, but it's -- it doesn't answer my question. I understand that you say there may have been matters that you could not recollect. You say that you were not focused and that you did not have an opportunity to correct mistakes. But my question is: Were you -- to the extent you were able to recall the matters that were put to you, were you truthful? Were you trying to tell the truth or were you trying to mislead or deceive the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Sir, I am declaring to this Tribunal that that statement was used by the Prosecution as a means of blackmail to make me appear before this Court. That's why I refused to be the Prosecution's witness, but I obeyed the subpoena sent to me by the Court. And I am here to speak the truth before this Court under the subpoena.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I would submit that you still have not answered my question. Could you please focus on the question and answer the question and then we can move on to other matters. The question is: Did you try to tell the truth in that interview? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Sir, I explained this issue. I cannot say that -- how truthful I was in that interview, whether it was true or not, because I never had a chance to look at it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry to persist on this point, but it's important to have answers to the questions before we can move on. The question is not whether it's accurate or not; it's not whether you may have made mistakes. The question is -- it has to do with your motivation. Were you trying to tell the truth in the interview were you not trying to tell the truth in the interview? If you could just answer that question. You've provided other explanations now, but if you could answer that question.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tried to tell the truth, but of course during the interview there were very provocative answers -- questions, sorry, asked of me and I tried to tell them that they were not giving me a chance to explain things. And at the end of the interview as far as I remember I clearly stated that something of the truth was stated, but not the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, can you please describe -- you've told us when and where -- you've told us when you were born and where you were born. Can you tell us how far you went in school, your education, please.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I finished the faculty of journalism and I am doing post-university studies at Pristina University for political sciences.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you go to high school?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I did my high school in Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And after your high school in Lipjan, did you go then to the faculty of journalism?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. I was imprisoned by the Serb occupiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before you were imprisoned - and I will ask you some questions about that - did you start schooling in the university?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I enrolled at Pristina University but couldn't continue my studies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you start in the university or did you not even have an opportunity to start?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I didn't have an opportunity to start.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that you were imprisoned; what year was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, please, what happened. How is it that you were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I was a member of clandestine organisations then which dealt with clandestine activities to ensure the recognition of the rights of the Albanian peoples in Kosova, like the other peoples of the former Yugoslavia. This clandestine organisation was working to ensure Kosova republic in the context of the Yugoslav Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did the -- did this clandestine organisation have a name?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. Popular Movement for the Republic of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was it known by any initials?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, LPRK.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did the name of that organisation change at some point?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, the change of the name occurred when I was doing my prison term.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately what year that name changed?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: To my recollection, in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did the name change to?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The word "Republic" was removed because at that time the Kosova Assembly had proclaimed the statement for Kosova and the name became LPK, Movement for -- Popular Movement for Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were imprisoned because you were a member of the LPRK, as it was known at that time. Were you charged with something in particular, with some particular activity?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I was accused for the organisation of the demonstrations in 1989 under Article 139, which was related to Article 114 of the Criminal Law of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was your sentence?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I was sentenced to 13 years of jail.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you serve 13 years in jail?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I served only five because after the changes that occurred in 1990 in the former Yugoslavia and the introduction of political pluralism the deed pertaining to Article 139 was removed and so I was sentenced only under Article 119 which was for political offences. So my sentence was reduced after the amnesty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So you were released from prison in 1994?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you served your prison sentence from 1989 to 1994?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: In several prisons, initially in Pristina jail. Then Gjurakovc and Dubrava in Kosova, and the last three years in Nis prison in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After you were released in 1994, were you a member of any political party or movement or organisation, either clandestine or public?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. After my release from prison I was engaged in public activities in the Democratic League of Kosova, which was known by the population as The Movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was that also known by any initials?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, LDK.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long were you a member of the LDK?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: For some six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened at the end of the six months?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: During all the time that I -- after my release, the occupy -- the occupiers, police and army, were exerting pressure on me. They detained me very often on the street. They called me to report to them and asking me to report every day at the police station in Lipjan; this prevented my political activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you explain a little further in what sense that prevented your political activity.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It prevented it because the police -- the Serb police forces didn't allow me to have -- didn't enable me to have the identity card, and the purpose for that was that every time the police stopped me they could maltreat me for not possessing that document, that identity card. And then sometimes they have called me for informative talks at Lipjan station, where they questioned me for a whole day and released me in the evening. This happened for two days. And they asked me to report there every day and I refused to obey that order, so they became more aggressive towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you were questioned for an entire day during these informative talks, were you mistreated?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. The very fact of me being there and questioned was a mistreatment, but they didn't mistreat me physically; psychologically, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did they question you about?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They questioned me about my political commitment and activity and the context of the LDK, its members whom they knew because they were public figures, they were known to all. They asked me whether they were engaged in some other clandestine activities. These were more or less the questions they asked of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did anybody ever think that you were cooperating with the Serb authorities, with the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, but the aim of the Serb forces when they detained people for these informative talks was to compromise the personality of the time, the political personalities. And I think this Court, this Tribunal, should bear in mind this fact that over 900.000 Albanians of Kosova were subjected to this treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly, that the aim was to compromise the personality of -- the political personalities? Can you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, because being present in those informative talks and their intention to have the politicians report to police stations on a daily basis aimed at spreading their notorious propaganda that such-and-such a person among the political personalities is our man or our collaborator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you know at the time it was happening in 1994/1995, did you know that that was their aim? Did you realise that at the time, that this was the aim of the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. These were obvious for us to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, in 1995 did you leave Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, in 1995 I left Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: And went to Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I can't be accurate, but it was I think the beginning of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Approximately how many months after you had been released from prison?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Maybe nine or ten months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you said that after six months you stopped being a member of the LDK. Before you left Kosovo, did you -- for Switzerland, did you join any other political organisation or movement, either clandestine or public?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I was a member of the Kosova Popular Movement even though I could not act as a member of this movement I still belonged, I pertained [as interpreted] to that movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that's the LPK?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why did you leave Kosovo to go to Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Because of the reasons I mentioned earlier, the great pressure brought to bear on me by the Serb violent apparatus, as well as other reasons which were economic reasons added to them. It is common knowledge that at that time in Kosova all the Albanian workers had been fired from institutions, be them political, economic, or educational and scientific institutions. And they were -- the young people were pressured to be recruited in the wars that Serbia was waging against the freedom-loving peoples of Yugoslavia, and there were over 500.000 youths, Albanian youths, who had left Kosova, and I was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you work in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, I was an asylum-seeker.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Before I was granted asylum in Switzerland, I stayed for nine months. Then after nine months, they granted me this asylum and I stayed some two or three years after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After you were granted asylum, were you able to work?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to work. But the Swiss policy was that we should start our integration into the life there and could attend language courses, German in my case, and vocational courses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you were working, what work did you do?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I did not work in Switzerland in the sense of getting income from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. Were you involved -- did you continue to be involved in the LPK in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. I began to be involved, unfortunately very little because of my financial situation. But at a later phase I became directly involved and I continued my activity in this political movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you describe what you did in this later phase, what kind of activities you participated in. And we're still talking about your time Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I dealt mainly with organisation of informative rallies for the citizens, Albanian citizens, who are immigrants in Germany, Switzerland, and other countries. We organised cultural and sports activity and such likes -- such like.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, could you briefly tell the Chamber what the -- what you understood the LPK to stand for. What did it advocate?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The LPK was a political organisation which was politically committed to the solution of the Albanian question, the political status for Kosova, and it conducted its public activity in the Western state countries, whereas its activity in Kosova was difficult and it was done underground. Mainly -- it was committed to the liberation of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: There's been some evidence in this trial about the LDK and the fact that the LDK took what might be described as a peaceful or pacifist approach to obtaining the liberation of Kosovo. Did the LPK, to your knowledge, take the same approach or a different approach? How would you describe the approach of the LPK?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The difference between these two organisations consisted in the fact that the LDK had as part of its political philosophy the peaceful movement which became actually a passive movement, pacifist movement, whereas the LPK was more active in its approach. Its programme didn't rule out the possibility for armed war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you first begin to hear about the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Even during my prison term in 1994 it was written about some communiques issued by the KLA, but more directly -- we talked with Nait Hasani who was my political cooperator, a man who I had shared a prison term in Dubrava prison. The talks we had amongst us were not very open because the risk was very great, but we talked about the activity of the KLA, the organisation of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when would you say, if you know, the KLA became publicly known in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The KLA became public in 1997 with a public appearance of three of its representatives following the fighting in Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was that an appearance at a funeral?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember where that was?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This happened in Drenica. I don't remember the name of the village, but I remember it was November 1997. I think it was the village of Llausha.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Buja, are you able to tell us what is the relationship, if any, between the LPK and the KLA at the end of 1997/beginning of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The organisation of LPK, as I [as interpreted] was organised in Switzerland and after the public appearance of the KLA, it mainly consisted of supporting the KLA politically and financially.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In Switzerland do you know who the leaders were of the LPK at the end of 1997/beginning of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who were they?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The president of the Kosova Popular Movement, the LPK, for the diaspora branch was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, you'll have to -- first of all, you'll have to repeat the name and I'll ask you, if you could, try to speak up a little bit more so the interpreters can hear what you're saying. So could you repeat the name of what the president of the LPK was in the diaspora.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The president of the LPK, the branch in diaspora was Fazli Veliju.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were there any other leaders of the LPK in Switzerland aside from the president?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, there were members of the Presidency and it had an executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember any of those names?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Of course I remember. Emrush Xhemajli, Bardhyl Mahmuti, Adem Grabovci, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, did you hold any position in the LPK at this time, at the end of 1997/beginning of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: In the general meeting of the diaspora branch, I was elected member of the LPK branch in the diaspora.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This happened in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was there a leader at this time of the LPK within Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There could have been, but I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to move forward in time to 1998. In 1998 did you leave Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember what month?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It was March.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We travelled from Switzerland to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you then go from Albania to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was it still March when you arrived in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, March.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, what made you decide to go on this trip at this time in March of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I was the person who insisted mostly for the members of the executive council to return to Kosova and engage in the movement in Kosova. The situation created in Kosova because the violent apparatus -- the Serb violent apparatus in Kosova had begun an operation in Drenica area, but what made me go to Kosova the most was the heroic fight of Adem Jashari, our legendary commander, and the sacrifice of the entire Jashari family. Of course to this we can also add the massacres that the Serb forces committed in other Drenica villages like the massacre in Likoshan and Qirez.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. When you decided to go in March of 1998, was that your decision or -- and this is with respect to the timing, the decision to go at that time, was it your decision or did anybody tell you that it was time to go?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The decision to go to Kosova was made by me, and as for the organised journey it was organised by others, by members of the LPK.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know Hashim Thaqi at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I knew him as a member of the Kosova Popular Movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you have any conversations with him before your decision to return to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We didn't have prior discussions, but we did discuss this on the day when I decided to return to Kosova I was informed that others were returning to Kosova and I of course informed my close friend and cooperator Agim Bajrami, I informed him we were heading to Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You say you were informed that others were returning to Kosova. Was it Hashim Thaqi who informed you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, it was Hashim Thaqi, Adem Grabovci and others, and of course my brother Agush Buja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: At that time, on that day that you made the decision to return to Kosovo, did you consider yourself a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I considered myself a member of the KLA from the moment I began with my activity to support the KLA financially and politically.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you tell us when that was. When was that moment?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This was the moment of my engagement in LPK to support the KLA financially and politically. This was in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you similarly consider Hashim Thaqi at that time in March of 1998 to be a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We couldn't consider him as a member of the KLA, but we could consider him as a member of the LPK who was also engaged in supporting the KLA politically and financially.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Had you heard about -- again, in March of 1998, had you heard about the existence of the General Staff of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, we were informed because at that time the KLA General Staff communiques were being published.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know who -- did you know at that time in March of 1998 who the members of the General Staff were?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Of course we didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know if Hashim Thaqi at that time was a member of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: At the time that you decided to go you said that you learned that others had decided to go, who else besides the people you've told us?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Amongst the others were Ismet Jashari, whom I knew from the political engagement in LPK. In Albania I met with Fehmi Lladrovci, Xhem Lladrovci, Sami Lushtaku and many others. Amongst them whom I'll later on know by name was Fatmir Limaj [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you first meet Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: My meeting with Fatmir Limaj was in Switzerland. I don't know how many times I met with him there, not frequently but it could have been once or twice. I then met with him on my journey to Albania and to Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that you met once or twice with Fatmir Limaj in Switzerland. Do you remember the first time you met with him in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. It could have been in the editorial board of the Zeri i Kosoves, Kosova Voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: As I said, I cannot remember the time of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember if it was in 1997? 1998? Before then?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It could have been in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did Fatmir Limaj have some role on the -- on that newspaper?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember the circumstances of the meeting, how it is that you came to meet at that editorial board of that newspaper?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't remember the circumstances of that meeting, but what I know is that many members of the movement, many compatriots, many Albanian immigrants in Switzerland, they would come to the editorial office. We would contact, maintained contacts with them, and we mainly conducted political discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was Fatmir Limaj, to your knowledge, a member of the LPK?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know and I can't say whether he was or he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was Fatmir Limaj living in the same place as Ismet Jashari?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know where Fatmir Limaj was living at the time in end of 1997/beginning of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you -- moving forward again to March of 1998 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps before you proceed, is that a convenient time?
