utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. I wasn't sure what the time was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We've had unusual hours because of the late start, but we'll resume again at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're having a break now and we'll resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I would just remind you again to please try to speak up when providing your answers. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, before the break I was going to ask you some further questions about March of 1998. You said that you had a conversation with Hashim Thaqi and learned that others were going to return to Kosovo at that time. When did you learn that Fatmir Limaj was also going to Kosovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I didn't say that it was only in conversation with Hashim Thaqi, but with others as well. As for Fatmir Limaj, I met him in Albania, and from Switzerland to Albania we travelled on the same plane.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were there others in your group on that flight from Switzerland to Albania besides you and Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It wasn't my group but it was a group to which I belonged as well. There was Adem Grabovci, Hashim Thaqi, Ismet Jashari, Agim Bajrami and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was Fehmi Lladrovci on that flight?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. I met with Fehmi Lladrovci in Albania. He came with several others from Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know the others that he came with from Germany?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Others came from Germany as well, including Sami Lushtaku. There were from other states as well which came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Which other states besides Germany and Switzerland? What other countries?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I can't know all the countries, but for sure from Austria and -- in one word from Western countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the group you were part of from Switzerland, you've given us some names. Can you tell us approximately how many people were in your group?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Ten to 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where exactly did you go in Albania? Where did you fly to?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: To Rinas airport in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you stay in Tirana or did you go somewhere else in Albania?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: In the beginning we stayed in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Tirana?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't remember how long. It could be that we spent a night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We set off towards the Albanian/Albanian border, Albanian/Kosova border.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Tirana, was the group that you've referred to from Germany that included Fehmi Lladrovci and Sami Lushtaku, were they already there or did they arrive after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know. We met with them at the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did the group that you were a part of from Switzerland, the 10 to 15 people, did you travel together from Tirana to the border?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were there any other people that joined that group in Tirana before you set off for the border?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What happened in Tirana before you left? Did you meet with anybody there, your group? And when I mean your group, the group you were a part of.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There were other people in Tirana as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who were the people in Tirana?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I -- amongst them my youngest brother was there as well, Lutfi Buja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was Emrush Xhemajli there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear that he was there? Did you learn that he was there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But did somebody tell you that he was there or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I cannot say what others said but what I have seen with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact you can say what others said and it's -- I appreciate that you see the distinction and it's important that you make the distinction for us in giving your answers between what you saw for yourself and from what you heard from others, but the Court can hear what you heard from others. So if you could answer the question: Did you learn from anybody else that Emrush Xhemajli was there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't remember learning about this from someone else and simply I didn't see Emrush Xhemajli there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you -- how about Xhavid Haliti? Did you see him there in Tirana before you set off for the border?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: To my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you know who he was at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: He was a member of the Presidency of the LPK; that's how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know if he had any role in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: At that time I didn't know about his role in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you learn later that he had a role in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: After the war. I learned about this after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Tirana, the group that you were a part of, did you receive instructions on where you should go or what you should do?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We didn't receive instructions. We were going to Kosova and we were interested in knowing the situation at the border, whether there were -- there was a great concentration of police and army forces, Serb police and army forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were you able to determine the situation at the border? Was anybody able to tell you what the situation at the border was?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We discussed this amongst each other. The situation at the border was quite difficult due to the concentration of the Serb forces there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you say "we discussed this amongst each other," are you talking about the members you are -- of the group you are part of or with others?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Mainly I discussed things with Agim Bajrami and several students who were there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the students, were they a part of the group from Switzerland or had they been in Tirana?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, they were studying in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were they members of the KLA, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, did you -- how was -- how was it decided where exactly you would go, how you would cross the border? Was this something that you decided amongst yourselves or was this something that was told to you? Were you given instructions on how you should travel to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I did not deal with these matters. There were others dealing with this matter. I didn't know the terrain. I wasn't familiar with the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who in your group dealt with this matter?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know who dealt with these matters but I know that the group set off together with others, and we had like a -- advanced guard unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did this advanced guard unit come from?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It was there on the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you learn -- you said you did not deal with these matters and you're not able to say who in your group did deal with these matters, but did you learn whether your group had received instructions or an order to make the trip to the border? And when I say "did you learn that," did you hear that? Were you told that? Did you come to know that at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: At that time there were persons who mainly dealt with entering from Albania to Kosova. I didn't know these people. We were told to go to the border and we did that. With -- by cars we went to the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you know who told your group to go to the border?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Xhavid Haliti came and said we could set off for the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before you went to the border did you -- were you given any weapons or uniforms or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you have any equipment?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. Up to the border we were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What happened at the border?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: At the border those who could find a uniform found a uniform and we got equipped with ammunition and weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, please, what it is exactly what you found at the border. Did you go to a village, a camp, or what -- where was it that you got this equipment and uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We went to a village and the weapons were given to us there and the ammunition boxes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you -- and then -- and then what happened? Did you then cross the border?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, we set off for the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you cross the border? Do you remember -- do you know what village or area of the border did you cross?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure because I don't remember exactly. Maybe it was the village of Vlon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you were told -- when your group was told that it was -- that you could go to the border and cross, were you also told where to go in Kosovo once you crossed the border?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you go after you crossed the border?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We were heading towards the Drenica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, the Drenica area is quite a large area. Were you heading in any more specific -- heading to any more specific place within Drenica?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We set off for Drenica and we were not yet familiar with the situation in Drenica, and we were not sure in which villages we could base ourselves because we didn't know which villages were already liberated by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you get into Kosovo, how many people are in your group?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Approximately 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And once you crossed the border, how were you travelling? Were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you travelling by car? Were you travelling by foot?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The major part of the journey on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long -- where in Drenica did you end up as a group, still as a group of 30? Where's the first village or town that you ended up in in Drenica?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I based myself in the village of Tice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did the entire group of 30 go to that village of Tice?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, because it is -- it was impossible for the entire group to stay in one village that did not have many inhabitants. So this group was dispersed in several villages of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did that occur? That's my question. Where did that occur? Where did your group break up into smaller groups?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to say where precisely because I was not familiar with the Drenica terrain. It could have been the village of Llausha, Tice, Likovc.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand you're not sure what village it occurred in. Can you describe how that occurred. You arrived in some place as a group of 30, and then how did it occur that you broke up into smaller groups? How was that decided? How did that happen, if you could describe that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Arrive -- having arrived in Drenica we saw KLA soldiers and we needed a place to settle so that we could spend the night and be ready to act the following day; therefore, we broke into smaller groups. Together with Fehmi Lladrovci I went to a house in Tice village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just the two of you went to that house?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There were two other soldiers whose names I don't remember, and I didn't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, at this time were you -- did you know one other by your names or did you use pseudonyms?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Some knew each other by names, but as of yet they didn't have pseudonyms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you spend in this village of Tice?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It could be three or four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what's the next thing that you did?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: During these days we discussed the organisation of the KLA, the situation with the population there, with -- about the tendencies of the Serb occupiers to set the limit of the KLA warfare to the territory of Drenica only, and the risk that this could pose considering the massacres and the uprising that had already occurred in 1945 in Drenica. The situation with the population there -- although I was there for different reason, I was there to deal with journalism to report as a war reporter directly from the field. Having faced the risk of the population, I decided to set off for Kosova and to organise guerrilla units in that part of Kosovo where I was familiar with the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, the discussions that you just described regarding the organisation of the KLA, the situation, were these discussions that the four of you had in Tice, the four soldiers, you, Fehmi Lladrovci, and the two others you can't remember, or were you having these discussions with other soldiers or other leaders of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We discussed with Hashim Thaqi as well and another person whose name I didn't know at the time. I spoke about this with Fehmi Lladrovci as well; with Fatmir Limaj, whose name I didn't know at the time; and with Agim Bajrami, whom I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said you didn't know Fatmir Limaj's name at that time. Did you know him by a pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. During the time I was in Tice village, I didn't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you learn his name -- or let me ask you a different question. Did you learn his name first or his pseudonym first?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: First I learned his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when did you learn his name?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I think it was this period of time during my stay in Tice, maybe three or four days after.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you had met Fatmir Limaj on one or two occasions in Switzerland. Are you saying that you didn't know his name when you met him in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I could have heard his name at that time when we met because he probably introduced himself. But I did not remember his name when we entered Kosova, because as I said I met many people at the editorial office of Zeri i Kosoves, Voice of Kosova, and it was difficult for me to remember all those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you learn his pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It depends which pseudonym you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, why don't you tell us which pseudonyms you are aware of.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Initially I knew him with the pseudonym Arben and Daja because his nephews called him, Daja, and we also called him Daja. And much later the Celiku pseudonym came into use.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you first hear the Celiku pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It could be May 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you said you were having these discussions with all these people, Fehmi Lladrovci, Fatmir Limaj, Hashim Thaqi. Are they staying in villages around Tice?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were staying in Tice, but I knew that they were staying in that territory which had smaller villages. There was also a wounded soldier as well -- in fact, there were two injured soldiers. One was -- had serious injuries and there was a medical centre there as well. So we would meet in Tice or in that medical centre or if I'm not mistaken here in Likovc because I'm not sure whether Likovc was there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Aside from the people you've mentioned that were part of your -- part of the group that you crossed the border with, were there other people who were based in Drenica who had been there before you arrived that you met with?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. There was a smaller part of soldiers who I saw when I arrived in Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember any of their names?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, because I couldn't know them by name and it was illogical for me to ask them for their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, how about pseudonyms? Do you know any of their pseudonyms?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, because I didn't ask. There was no need for me to ask them with the exception of one pseudonym, Dhjeqi, meaning number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever learn who this -- the name of this person Dhjeqi or number 10?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, later I did learn the name of number 10. His name was Rexhep Selimi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where was Rexhep Selimi based when you arrived there in March of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know where he was based, but I know that we met in the area I met -- I mentioned earlier, Tice, Likovc, or some other village which I can't name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he appear at that time to be a commander or at a higher level in the area where you were, Rexhep Selimi?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I couldn't know what -- at what level of organisation he belonged. I simply regarded him as a soldier of the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You saw -- your testimony is that you saw him as a soldier no different from all the other soldiers that you saw there from the KLA? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, that's my testimony. We had -- we were wearing uniforms. We had weapons. We couldn't tell one soldier from the other. It wasn't easy to tell someone from the appearance, if he were at a higher level. But talks with him showed that he had very good political preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you learn if he had any contacts with the General Staff of the KLA, any communication with the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know about Rexhep Selimi, but in talks with Hashim Thaqi I found out he had contacts with the General Staff. At least this is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, what happened after these discussions that lasted -- I believe you testified for three or four days. What's the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I didn't say they lasted three, four days. I said that during these three, four days we held talks. Some once or twice with Hashim Thaqi. Once with Dhjeqi, number 10. And from the very first meeting I asked to be sent in the direction of the place where I was born, which I knew better, whose people I was familiar with, that is, in Lipjan and Shtime municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And after those three or four days, were you sent there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: After three, four days we did leave in the direction of the municipalities that we thought of organising the guerrilla units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But my question is: Were you -- you said that you asked to go to the area where you were born. After you asked to go, were you sent there, were you told to go there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, they approved it. Hashim Thaqi approved my proposal to be engaged in the military organisation, to start organising a guerrilla unit in the place I knew well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you told specifically what areas you should organise guerrilla units?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. It was my request, as I said, that was approved by Hashim Thaqi to go to the area which I knew. At the time, we couldn't define the operational zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, that wasn't my question. My question was: When it was approved by Hashim Thaqi to go to the area you knew, what area was that? Is it just your village? Is it villages around your area? Is there any particular area that you were tasked to go to?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Lipjan municipality is not a village; it's a municipality that comprises several villages, as the case is today with Shtime and Lipjan municipalities. We couldn't simply concentrate on a single, small village like my village was called Bujan. And I couldn't, as I said, concentrate my work only there because the danger in that case was very great. It was -- the village was situated on a plain. It was very dangerous for us to work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So you were only -- your task when you left was to go to organise in Lipjan municipality, not any other municipalities, just Lipjan?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I had decided myself to go to Shtime municipality, which I had some in-laws, a person whom I trusted to stay with this family, from where I could work for the organisation of the guerrilla unit. I thought to do that through people who were politically involved in the Lipjan municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was Fatmir Limaj given any task at this time to go somewhere and organise or do something else?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I can't say whether he was given any tasks, but from conversations we have had with him and Agim Bajrami, Fatmir Limaj had expressed his wish to be working in Malisheve municipality area from where he was from actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And after he expressed his wish, was that wish approved by Hashim Thaqi?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: To my recollection together with Fatmir, Agim Bajrami, Ismet Jashari, Haxhi Shala, we left to go to the respective area where they were familiar with and where they had people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That wasn't my question -- or that wasn't an answer to my question. My question was: Did Fatmir Limaj ask to go organise in Malisevo and that was that approved by Hashim Thaqi? Did he say, Yes, go organise in Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This time I would object to the leading nature of the question. Mr. Whiting is driving towards obtaining approval. He can ask him how Hashim Thaqi responded to the wish made by Mr. Limaj or by anybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You told -- you testified that Fatmir -- it was Fatmir Limaj's wish to go to organise in Malisevo. My question is: Did he put that wish to Hashim Thaqi the way you put your wish to Hashim Thaqi? Did he do that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know whether he did that. I do know that I myself asked to be allowed to go to the area which I knew well and I could work for the organisation of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So do you know if -- do you know if Fatmir Limaj was given a task, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I know that he was given a task of accompanying us or showing us the way from Drenice area to the area of Malisheve municipality, which he knew well up to the border of that area and to the border of the area that I knew well. Whereas, I would accompany Agim Bajrami towards Kacanik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did that trip take to go from where you were in Drenica to Malisevo municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Our -- we travelled always during night because of the danger of Serb forces. So to my recollection we slept in a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But how -- but how long did the trip take from Drenica to Malisevo municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Several hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you go in Malisevo municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: If I'm not wrong it was Pagarushe village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who was in the group again that went to Pagarushe village?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It was myself, Fatmir Limaj, Ismet Jashari, Agim Bajrami, and Haxhi Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was any person a leader of that group or in charge of that group?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: In the sense of a command, no. But as I said earlier, the person who was supposed to show us the way because he knew the area well was Fatmir up to Pagarushe but not in the sense of any chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you -- you said it took you a few hours to get to Pagarushe. And then where did you go, did you spend -- where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: After Pagarushe village, Agim Bajrami and myself would continue the way towards the place we had set out for. We went to Klecke village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it was just the two of you who went to Klecke village?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, the two of us. Myself and Agim Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you go in Klecke village?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We went to the nephews of Fatmir, Sadik Shala. At that time I didn't know him by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We went there because we wanted to take Sadik, a person from that family, to escort us in the -- on the road that we didn't know from Klecke to Ribare village of the municipality I knew well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But did somebody tell you to go to Sadik Shala's house and pick him up or was that your idea?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It was not my idea because I didn't know Sadik Shala or his family. It was Fatmir who told us because he was their uncle. He knew the family. So he told us to go to Klecke to contact this family and to ask one of the -- his nephews to escort us to the village where we wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you spend in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: In Klecke we didn't stay more than an hour. We just contacted Sadik Shala and he came with us to accompany us through the villages of Shale, Blinaje, to Ligore [phoen] village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you one question. When you were in Pagarushe, how long did you stay in Pagarushe?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: In Pagarushe we stayed one night; the next we travelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you said you went with Sadik Shala to the villages of Shale, Blinaje. Where did you end up?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Until Ribare we were accompanied by Sadik; he had acquaintances there because it was after midnight when he arrived. He stayed with the people he knew, whereas myself and Agim Bajrami continued our way to our native village and we managed to reach my home by early morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And this is your home in Bujan?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Bujan?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We stayed there about two days. I thought that through my elder brother, Rame Buja, I could start establishing contacts with people whom I knew in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And after two days where did you go?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: After two days we set out for where I had thought of basing myself, Bulapovc [phoen] in the family of Mevbajovc [phoen] where I could continue my unit to organise a guerrilla unit and I held talks with people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What's the name of the village again you went to? Bulapovc?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Mullapolc.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's what I thought. And that's in what municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Shtime municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I stayed there in March, April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, at this time you -- you've testified that you left Fatmir Limaj in Pagarushe village. Is that right? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know where he went after that, after Pagarushe village?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We had agreed to keep contact through his nephews in Klecke, and I believed that Fatmir Limaj would be settled in Klecke and that we would have -- keep contacts with the couriers, his nephew and my brother Avni Buja from Bujan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you have any understanding about what he was going to be doing in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I had the understanding that he, too, would start work for the organisation of the guerrilla unit as I was going to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who else besides Fatmir Limaj went to Klecka, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Together with him I think went also Ismet Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what about the Haxhi Shala. You mentioned his name before. Do you know where he went?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I don't know where he went because he could move freely because he was not persecuted by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that you had agreed to keep in contact by courier with Fatmir Limaj in Klecka. Can you tell us, what was the purpose of those contacts?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The purpose of these contacts was that in case I needed to go to Drenica where I could contact Hashim Thaqi, through couriers we could set up the meeting time so that Fatmir Limaj could organise my escort up to Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was there any other purpose or was the only purpose to arrange meetings with Hashim Thaqi, if that's what you wanted to do?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The form of organisation of the KLA at that time, the way I saw it, was the General Staff and the guerrilla units. As a man who was supposed to organise a guerrilla unit, I had to keep in touch with the General Staff through Hashim Thaqi. That was the purpose of my trip there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But my question is about your contacts with Fatmir Limaj. Did you stay in -- you've testified that you stayed in contact -- you agreed to stay in contact with Fatmir Limaj in order -- for the purpose of arranging meetings with Hashim Thaqi. Was that the only reason to stay in contact with Fatmir Limaj or were there other reasons?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Meetings and -- in Albanian there are two words for meeting. It means personal meeting and meetings. So the purpose of the meeting was for us to keep in touch for needs that I mentioned earlier. That's why I wanted to contact the Hashim Thaqi in order for me to get in touch with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But could you communicate with Hashim Thaqi through Fatmir Limaj? In other words, a courier would send a message to Hashim Thaqi -- I mean to Fatmir Limaj who would then communicate with the General Staff and then return with information? Would that happen?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, because that couldn't happen because the time we are talking about was a very hard, difficult time. We were at the beginning of the organisation of the guerrilla units. So I had for many reasons, for many needs I had to set out for meeting Fatmir Limaj and then for Drenica where I could get clear instruction through Hashim Thaqi from the General Staff about my further actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, can you explain for us why you would have to first meet Fatmir Limaj and then go meet Hashim Thaqi to get the instructions. Why that step, meeting Fatmir Limaj? What was the purpose of that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Because the purpose was that I couldn't travel on my own. I didn't know the area to Drenice. I knew only Shtime and Lipjan municipality area, whereas Fatmir knew the area in Malisheve municipality which was linked to Llapushe territory or Drenice area and he was, as I said earlier, familiar with that area. So he could accompany me. It was a time of great dangers for us to move about without knowing the terrain well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I don't want to belabour this point, but I do want to be clear. So it your testimony that Fatmir Limaj's only role, then, was to help you travel in making contact with Hashim Thaqi so you could communicate with the General Staff? His only role was assist you on your travel. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever communicate with Hashim Thaqi or the General Staff through Fatmir Limaj? If you understand my question.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I tried to communicate through Fatmir Limaj, but my first meeting with Fatmir Limaj failed; it was supposed to be in April. I managed to contact him at the end of April 1998 for him to accompany me, as I said earlier, on this trip; but Fatmir Limaj and Ismet Jashari were injured and the great concentration of the Serb forces prevented me from going to Drenica. And all my trip was -- became possible only -- it was not in vain because there I met a soldier who had come from Germany and he was willing to come and help in the organisation of guerrilla unit in Ferizaj. So I had -- I kept contacts with Hashim Thaqi through telephone in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood my question. My question is: In March and April did you ever have a courier go to Fatmir Limaj for Fatmir Limaj to get information from Hashim Thaqi or the General Staff to then pass back to you; in other words, communicate with Hashim Thaqi or the General Staff that way, by first asking Fatmir Limaj to get the information and then waiting for the response from Fatmir Limaj. Did that ever happen in March or April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, this didn't happen in March, April, or later because the purpose of my contacts with Fatmir Limaj through the courier in April was jeopardised because my brother and his nephew wanted -- we were supposed to go to Klecke and from there these soldiers might accompany me to Drenica where I could contact Hashim Thaqi, but this didn't come true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is probably a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We then adjourn for the day, resuming at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 4th day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 25
